title: Multi-bot solo — 3 bots, one of each personality
notes: S139 added three visually-distinct bot personalities (hunter / coward / miner) but solo only spawned one bot per round. With three slots the player faces the full palette + AI behaviour mix every match: hunter chases, coward hides, miner farms blocks — each unmistakable by colour + accessory.

Scope: solo profile only. Connected mode keeps the single server-owned bot path (server-side AI doesn't know about local multi-bot). Round-resolve already handles n bombers via the 'one alive' rule, so multi-bot rounds end when only one bomber survives — battle-royale-shaped.

Personality assignment is stable per page load: bot.1 → hunter, bot.2 → coward, bot.3 → miner. The S139 random session pick still affects the URL-less default path (lets a future override re-shuffle), but the default is now a deterministic one-of-each so every solo round shows all three variants.

stories.title: makeKaboomRecipe handles bot.2 + bot.3 with the same personality-override path
stories.summary: examples/kaboom-crew/src/kaboom-recipe.ts — match any `bot.\d+` id instead of the exact 'bot.1' literal, then apply the personality palette + accessory when personality is provided. bot.N without personality falls back to 'rose' (legacy). player.1 still gets 'sky'.
verification: acceptance: examples/kaboom-crew/src/kaboom-recipe.ts replaces 'ownerId === bot.1' with the regex /^bot\.\d+$/, so bot.2/bot.3/etc follow the same personality-override path as bot.1. backward compat preserved — bot.N without personality keeps the 'rose' fallback. Existing 'sky'/'rose' tests still pass.

stories.title: Bootstrap spawns + tunes all three bots (one of each personality)
stories.summary: examples/kaboom-crew/bootstrap.ts — replace the bot.1-only spawn + difficulty patches with a loop over MULTI_BOT_ASSIGNMENT = [{id: 'bot.1', personality: 'hunter'}, {id: 'bot.2', personality: 'coward'}, {id: 'bot.3', personality: 'miner'}]. For each: difficultyComponentPatch + makeKaboomRecipe + spawnBomberFor. Applied both on initial attach AND on resetRound. Connected mode still deletes bot.1 only (server owns it); bot.2 + bot.3 don't exist server-side.
verification: acceptance: examples/kaboom-crew/bootstrap.ts now loops over MULTI_BOT_ASSIGNMENT (bot.1→hunter, bot.2→coward, bot.3→miner) at all three call sites (resetRound, initial attach, difficulty-cycle restart). Each bot gets its own BotBrain personality + difficulty patch + recipe + bomber-tree spawn. renderer's resolveForOwner closure uses a Map<id,personality> built from the same assignment. Connected mode deletes all 3 solo bot ids (server owns bot.1 only). The demo-30s deterministic test still passes after explicitly removing bot.2/bot.3 (it's a designed 1v1 duel test).

stories.title: Unit test: bot.2 + bot.3 with personality get distinct palettes + accessories
stories.summary: examples/kaboom-crew/tests/unit/recipe-personality.test.ts (extend) — call makeKaboomRecipe('bot.2', 'coward') / ('bot.3', 'miner') and assert paletteName + single accessory match. bot.2 without personality returns base seed-driven recipe (no forced 'rose' fallback needed since we relax the exact-match check — verify the regex/check is intentional).
verification: acceptance: examples/kaboom-crew/tests/unit/recipe-personality.test.ts adds the S141 case — bot.2+coward→slate+visor, bot.3+miner→sand+cap, bot.2 without personality→rose fallback. 9/9 recipe-personality tests pass.
